> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e11d9006cdc9548dbb1f3883687fdbe2bfe21f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b2722e362a4ced348e9ae1df0867de932492af7e` — the merge of head `bd79104296c7cb6b81710c9312d5f92e102df6af` into base `2e11d9006cdc9548dbb1f3883687fdbe2bfe21f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b2722e362a4ced348e9ae1df0867de932492af7e && git checkout b2722e362a4ced348e9ae1df0867de932492af7e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2e11d9006cdc9548dbb1f3883687fdbe2bfe21f7 bd79104296c7cb6b81710c9312d5f92e102df6af && git checkout -B drift-repro 2e11d9006cdc9548dbb1f3883687fdbe2bfe21f7 && git merge --no-ff bd79104296c7cb6b81710c9312d5f92e102df6af

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e11d9006cdc9548dbb1f3883687fdbe2bfe21f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2e11d9006cdc9548dbb1f3883687fdbe2bfe21f7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION — `Check Changeset` is red by design on this PR.** `domain:engine` seat 2 · `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX` · 2026-10-11T20:43Z.

- **The gate:** `check-empty-changeset.mjs`'s foreign-changeset refusal (and route 0 of `Require a changeset`) in the `Check Changeset` job of `pr-automation.yml`.
- **Why it is red:** commit `9e9aa0b7af` rewrites one parenthetical of the pending `.changeset/22739-import-reference-target-exposure.md`, a note this PR did not add. The sentence said a protocol without `getMetaItem` "(plugin-auth's identity import …) is not judged"; #22800 (PR #22866, `f9ebb7dd31`) made that false, and restoring it would ship a false sentence in the next CHANGELOG. Carried here per #22800's ACCEPT (6111874171).
- **Why it may land red:** the gate's own source names this class red by design; `Check Changeset` runs on `pull_request` only, not on `merge_group`, and is not a required context. A same-head contract-tier record confirms the corrected sentence before this seat arms the queue.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd79104296c7cb6b81710c9312d5f92e102df6af`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, on the card (#22823: body, release 6110112147, claim 6112207746, os-dev-report 6113489644, file-surface addendum 6113535816), the PR (body, the seat's DELIBERATE CORRECTION note 6113547162, the docs-drift comment, 7 files, 4 commits), the net diff against `origin/main` (merge base `75b6d6a048`; 7 files, +341 / −8, none generated, none governed: `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success), the check-runs on the head, and the `origin/main` files the brief names. #22800's ACCEPT 6111874171 and its merge `f9ebb7dd31` read as cited context. Classes, positions and functions only.

**Check-runs on the head, at the final read:** 26 success, 3 skipped (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke`), 1 failure (`Check Changeset`, by design, judged in ③), and **4 still in progress: `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`.** `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:error-code-provenance`, `check:system-context-census`, `check:error-status-conformance`, `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`), the four `Type Check` jobs, `Temporal Conformance`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (all three), `Test Core (1/6)` and `(4/6)` are green. The new runtime test file rides a `Test Core` shard, so this PASS stands on the four named shards completing green; a red one re-opens the verdict.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set change the diff implies: one narrowing, at two arms of one function, `callData` (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`), for a non-system caller only. Public-surface change: none. `callData` is not on the runtime entry (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts` exports nothing from `action-execution`), `resolveWriteResponseSchema` keeps its signature (docblock extended), the spec change is two value-only rows in an existing const, and the core change is a test file. Nothing widens anywhere in the diff.

1. **The query fallback refusal — right.** The new `refuseUnservedRelationTargets` is called inside the `if (ql)` branch of the `query` / `find` arm, after the fallback's own unservable-key refusal and before `ql.find`, on `bag.where`, which is the `where` the engine was already handed through `findOpts(bag)`. The data door branch above it (`protocol.findData`) is before the fallback and unchanged.
2. **The aggregate arm refusal — right, as the bounded in-place fix the file-surface addendum accepted on the card.** The call sits before `engine.aggregate`, on `params.where`, the `where` the arm already forwarded. The arm takes no protocol service, so it is the engine's door on every assembly, which makes it the more reachable of the two positions (the HTTP MCP aggregate tool reaches it); the claim's function-level description now reads "and its aggregate arm" on the card. The ask covers the top-level `where` only, the form #22777's stdio bridge pins for its aggregate verb; the dev's statement that the engine lowers relation conditions in `where` and never inside an aggregation's own filter is inherited from that pinned form and was not re-read here (the engine's lowering is outside this review's read set). Named, not a finding.
3. **The envelope — right.** `unservedRelationTargetError` is the data door's `refuseUnservedRelationTarget` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) field for field: `code` and `status` by the gate's verdict (`OBJECT_API_DISABLED` 404 for `apiEnabled: false`, else `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` 405), `object` the target (not the addressed object), `param` the condition's position spelled `where.LOOKUP` (the stdio bridge's spelling; the data door spells its own REST parameter, `filter.LOOKUP`), `allowed` only on a 405, the effective operation set (the test pins a `create`-only whitelist answering the derived pair, as the data door's `effectiveOperationsArray` does). The two message templates and the consequence tail are the data door's own text. The addressed-object gate of the same function throws a bare `statusCode`/`message` object; the target refusal does not copy that shape, and that is right: the protocol path's refusal of the same condition already reaches the dispatcher through `callData` as this `Error` envelope, so the fallback now gives the answer the path it stands in for gives (`check:error-status-conformance` and `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` ride in `Lint & Repo Gates`, green).
4. **System callers — right for this door, residual named.** The bypass is decided once, `exposureGated = !executionContext?.isSystem`, the flag the addressed-object gate already read, and both calls of the target ask are under it. That is the stdio bridge's rule too (`enforceApiExposure` returns on `isSystem`), and it keeps `callData`'s system-context census row describing one decision (`check:system-context-census` in `Lint & Repo Gates`, green; the test's system-context control reaches the engine). Residual: the data door judges a system context for the same condition and this door does not; that split pre-exists for the addressed object and this PR does not move it.
5. **The protocol path untouched — right.** Only context lines of the `findData` branch appear in the diff; the test pins that with a protocol service resolved `findData` receives the query verbatim and `find` is never called.
6. **One gate and one walker — right.** The gate is `checkApiExposure`, the function the addressed object was already judged by in this file; no new decision function is written. `RELATION_CONDITION_TARGET_ACTION` is the action name `query` handed to that gate (what the stdio bridge's `GATED_ACTIONS.query` hands its gate), and `RELATION_CONDITION_TARGET_OPERATION` is read off the spec's `DATA_ACTION_TO_API_OPERATION` and used only in the message; the data door's own constant is the same `list`. The walker is `relationConditionSites`, imported from `@objectstack/core` (exported from core's entry; `@objectstack/core` is already a `workspace:*` dependency of `@objectstack/runtime`, so `check:undeclared-dep-imports` has nothing to say), fed the filtered object's `fields` map and the raw filter, as both other doors feed it. No second walk exists in runtime. The field map and each target's declaration come from the existing `resolveWriteResponseSchema` (engine registry first, then metadata, `undefined` when neither), and the new function falls open on `undefined` as `checkApiExposure` does; a plain id comparand or an operator-only bag on a lookup key is no site, pinned by a control.
7. **The census pin's row-10 handling — right.** `CALLERS` in `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` is keyed on files that call the arbiter `referenceTargetOf`; `callData` never calls it (the target is resolved inside `relationConditionSites`), so a row would be refused by the pin's own stale-caller check. Row 10 is named in the docblock's "what the discriminator does NOT see" paragraph in the shape rows 8 (#22777) and 9 (#22800) already take there, held by the runtime's own pin (`action-execution-calldata-relation-target-exposure.test.ts`, named), and the `relation-condition-sites.ts` row's reason now names all three doors in place of "both doors". The pin's arbiter-call scan is unaffected (no new caller, no stale one).
8. **The two ledger rows — right.** `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` and `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` are added inside the `@objectstack/runtime` block of `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` (`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`), which listed neither before; the four blocks that already list them (`rest`, `metadata-protocol`, `service-analytics`, `mcp`) are untouched, so the registered set is unchanged and the rows are provenance only, with a comment naming the stamping function and both arms. `check:error-code-provenance` is in `Lint & Repo Gates`, green; the dev's reverse-verification (two stamp sites named with the rows removed) is consistent with that.

Tests, read against the diff: 13 cases in the new runtime file; the four refused classes (`apiEnabled: false`; whitelists of `create` only, empty, `get` only) at the top level and under a combinator on the fallback, the same four on aggregate, each asserting the full envelope and that the engine verb was never called; two served controls reaching the engine with `where` unchanged on both arms; the plain-id control; the system control; the protocol-path pin. The ablation legs (A: fallback call; B: aggregate call) are the dev's; CI's `Test Core` shards are the verdict on the file.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/runtime` `minor`, `.changeset/22823-calldata-fallback-relation-exposure.md` — right.** The diff narrows `callData`'s accept set at the two arms for non-system callers; the changeset carries `fix(runtime)!:`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the BREAKING line, the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason (read and accepted by `check-adr-0087-registration` in the `Check Changeset` job, visible in its log; its "not on the export surface" claim holds against the runtime entry), FROM and TO matching the two positions and the envelope, a migration (filter on the lookup's stored id, or grant `list` on the related object) matching the code's own consequence text, Bindings matching ① 3, 4 and 6, and the measured producers with the NOT MEASURED bound. `minor` for a narrowing is the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major` in the same job: "narrowing — a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships minor").
- **`@objectstack/spec` `patch`, `.changeset/22823-spec-ledger-runtime-exposure-codes.md` — right.** Two value-only rows in an existing array literal; no export, schema, type or generated artifact moves. The no-major gate's named residual (a second widening graded `patch` beside the `minor` would escape it) is answered by the diff: the spec change accepts nothing, and nothing else in the diff widens.
- **No `@objectstack/core` changeset — right.** Its only change is a test file.
- **`Clause-②:` line — consistent.** PR body line 2 `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the runtime changeset's line 7 `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the claim 6112207746 `Clause-②: no` with the narrowing arm stated as its next bullet. One declaration, one arm, matching the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none in the os-dev-report.

`deviations`, each:
1. **File surface widened (spec ledger rows plus spec changeset; the aggregate arm)** — answered on the card: the file-surface addendum 6113535816 added both to the claim (cross-lane `domain:spec` as the ledger-append class; the aggregate arm under the bounded in-place exemption). Both judged right in ① 2 and ① 8.
2. **Dispatch "stop on a breach" versus the role file's bounded fix** — answered: every breach was declared in the report and the PR body, and the seat accepted both in the addendum. No silent widening.
3. **Refusal envelope (the data door's, not the addressed gate's bare object)** — answered, right (① 3).
4. **System context skips the target ask** — answered, right for this door, residual named (① 4).
5. **Branch not merged with `origin/main`** — answered: `main` has moved further since the report; GitHub reports the PR mergeable, and CI computed on the merge of the head into the current base (the docs-drift comment names that merge commit), so the derived gates measured the merged tree. The only shared file is the ledger, in a different package block.
6. **Commit trailers** — a repo-convention matter with no bearing on the contract axes; the session-URL trailer and the model-free co-author line are present on 9e9aa0b7af as read.
7. **`check-empty-changeset` red by design** — the DELIBERATE CORRECTION, judged below.
8. **Cleanup** — the dev's statement about its worktree; nothing in the diff to judge.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each:
1. **`relationConditionSites`'s docblock (`packages/core/src/utils/relation-condition-sites.ts`) still says two doors share no other package** — answered as a note, not a defect: comment only, outside the claim's surface; the pin's `CALLERS` row for that file now names three doors, so the drift is confined to the core source's own docblock. Carrier: the next family PR that touches `packages/core/src/utils/`, at the seat's choice.
2. **`callData`'s addressed-object gate reads the metadata service only, while the target ask (and the engine's lowering) reads the engine registry first** — escalated to the adopting seat as a measure-first question, not filed here: a read-only inference about the pre-existing addressed gate on a composition whose metadata slot does not carry the engine's objects, NOT MEASURED on a real composition, so not yet a class (a) filing under Prime Directive 10. This PR does not widen it; the target ask reads the schema the engine's lowering reads, which is the right source for the target. The seat decides whether a measurement card is worth its cost.

**The DELIBERATE CORRECTION (the seat's PR note 6113547162; PR body section "Deliberate correction"; carried from #22800's ACCEPT 6111874171).** `Check Changeset` is red for exactly one reason: `check-empty-changeset.mjs`'s foreign-changeset refusal naming `.changeset/22739-import-reference-target-exposure.md` (the job log's single error line; the same job's ADR-0087 registration and no-major steps pass). Commit `9e9aa0b7af` is one file, one line (+1 / −1), and the net diff of that file against `origin/main` is that same single line, inside "Bindings", first bullet. Judged clause by clause:

- Old text: "a protocol without it (plugin-auth's identity import, whose reads run under the system identity) is not judged." New text: "a protocol without it is not judged (plugin-auth's identity import carries the reader since #22800)."
- Clause (i), "a protocol without it is not judged" — the rule, unchanged in meaning from the old main clause, and true on `origin/main`: `f9ebb7dd31`'s only `packages/core` change is the TSDoc of `import-runner.ts`, which was corrected there in the same direction ("carries it like every other caller (#22800)"); the runtime behaviour for a protocol lacking `getMetaItem` is as #22739 shipped it.
- Clause (ii), "plugin-auth's identity import carries the reader since #22800" — true on `origin/main`: `f9ebb7dd31` is an ancestor of `origin/main`, and its hunk in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts` binds one `metaReader` (the import's `getMetaItem`) into both the parser and the run protocol; #22800's own note (`.changeset/22800-identity-import-exposure.md`, TO) states it in the same words, "the run protocol carries the same reader the parser is handed (one binding, so whenever a cell is a reference its target is judged)". So the old parenthetical's example is false on `main`, and restoring it would ship a false sentence in the generated CHANGELOG — the gate's own text for this class says not to restore.
- The dropped reason, "whose reads run under the system identity" — right to drop: #22800's note says the decision takes no caller and the system identity is no exemption, so keeping that clause would misstate why the import was once unjudged.
- Nothing else in the file moves: front matter (`@objectstack/core` `minor`), title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 marker, FROM, TO, the other two Bindings, the Fix line and the measured producers are byte-identical to `main`.

The correction is confirmed. Per the seat's note, `Check Changeset` runs on `pull_request` only and is not a required context; this record is the same-head confirmation that note asked for, and the queue leg does not re-run that gate.

Advisory, no action: the docs-drift comment lists nine hand-written pages naming `callData` or the ledger; the diff edits no doc, the behaviour added is the refusal those pages already describe for the data door, and `Flag docs affected by code changes` is green.

The four `Test Core` shards pending at the record's final read have since concluded: on this head all six `Test Core` shards and all seven required contexts are `success`; 31 success, 3 skipped, 1 failure (`Check Changeset`, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION judged above).
